title: Signal palette: onboarding regression cartography and remediation scenarios
content:
Summary
This is a working deep-dive into the recent onboarding regression signals we observed for the external-chat prompt suite (v3). The doc synthesizes error clusters discovered across the seed eval and live shadow traffic, defines a compact set of failure archetypes (the "signal palette"), and proposes low-risk, high-ROI mitigations + rollout steps to restore parity while preserving cost/latency targets. This is intentionally a pragmatic, patch-forward doc — we prioritize quick detection + safe fallbacks; longer-term solutions (retraining/ft) are tracked separately.

Scope and motivation
- Models: primary: rdw-instruct-13B-q4 (quant), fallback: rdw-instruct-13B-fp16, comparison baseline: open-13B-v2.
- Inputs: onboarding eval prompt sets (seeded conversation templates, 2.5k examples) + 48 hours of shadow traffic from hosted-api routes /chat-beta.
- Observed problem: a ~6.8% relative increase in end-to-end regression rate on onboarding eval (failure defined as automated eval mismatch + human anchor flag) after model swap on 2024-10-14. Several downstream customer feature tests also showed increased mismatch.

Methods used for clustering and signal extraction
- Features: token-level perplexity delta vs baseline, response length ratio, presence/absence of expected entities (regex-based), semantic embedding distance (SBERT) between expected answer and candidate, guardrail trigger flags.
- Dimensionality reduction: UMAP (n_neighbors=30, min_dist=0.1) for visualization and density-preserving layout.
- Clustering: HDBSCAN on UMAP embedding; stability tested across subsamples and feature ablations.
- Representative slicing: grouped by prompt archetype (instruction-heavy, Q&A short, multi-step reasoning, numeric-tabular, hallucination-prone).
- Sanity checks: manual review of 120 cluster exemplars; annotated precision/recall of cluster labels vs human labels ~0.78/0.72.

Discovered failure archetypes (signal palette) — concise descriptions + examples
1) Context drop (short): model truncates earlier system/context when user message is long, losing required facts.
   - Symptom: answer omits required entity referenced earlier in conversation; semantic distance high; low perplexity increase.
   - Representative prompt: multi-turn system message with behavioral constraints followed by a long user paste.
2) Attributive drift (attribution errors): model attributes actions/events to wrong entities or fabricates timestamps/owners.
   - Symptom: presence of temporal or ownership hallucinations; guardrail flags not firing.
3) Numeric instability (tables & conversions): incorrect arithmetic or wrong unit conversions in multi-step numeric prompts.
   - Symptom: short plausible-sounding but incorrect numbers; high token-level perplexity; often on longer numeric chains.
4) Overly terse safe-mode (hallucination-avoidance overshoot): model returns a maximally safe "I don't know" on prompts where it previously produced acceptable answers.
   - Symptom: fidelity drop with lower hallucination rate; surfaced by our fidelity/utility delta metric.
5) Style collapse on persona prompts: model loses persona tone and returns neutral generic text, breaking product UX tests.

Rootmap hypotheses (why clusters emerged after the swap)
- Kernel-selection mismatch in quant path: certain attention kernel combos used by the quantized runtime produce subtle context propagation differences under long-context patterns.
- Decoding default change: temperature/typical-p settings shifted on the deployed variant (operator config drift in the deployment manifest).
- Training data gap amplified: the quant variant was evaluated on short-context bench but not long-dense-context templates we use in onboarding.
- Prompt-binding fragility: small differences in tokenizer alignment after quant/compile stage cause rare tokenization splits that alter instruction markers.

Mitigation proposals (ranked by estimated effort vs impact)
- Tier 0: Immediate low-risk server-side mitigations (0–48 hrs)
  1) Route sensitive prompt archetypes (multi-step numeric, long context) to the fp16 variant by policy rule: route by prompt tag detect (regex + length threshold). Impact: high; cost delta: moderate. Rollback safe.
  2) Restore previous decoding defaults for the deployed quant model (temp/typical) via config patch. Impact: medium; risk: low.
  3) Add targeted post-generation reranker for numeric assertions: run a lightweight verifier (unit conversion library + integer sanity checks) and prefer candidate that passes checks. Impact: medium; cost: low.
- Tier 1: Medium-term prompt scaffolding and deterministic guards (3–14 days)
  1) Prompt scaffolds: for long-context prompts, inject an explicit "context-anchor" line (single token anchor + short summary) generated client-side or by preprocessor. This reduces context-drop risk without heavy compute.
  2) Tokenization check: create a small CI that verifies tokenization invariants between fp16 and quant build on a corpus of 10k onboarding prompts; block quant builds that change important instruction token boundaries.
  3) Expand eval harness with numeric micro-tests (small deterministic calculators) to catch numeric instability during model onboarding.
- Tier 2: Engineering + modeling changes (2–6 weeks)
  1) Micro-finetune on a compact long-context instruction set (3–5k cases) focusing on anchor retention and numeric stability; evaluate with strict regression gates.
  2) Quantization kernel fallback: add per-layer heuristics in the compilation pipeline to preserve fp behavior for attention layers flagged by CI. More invasive but durable.

Quick rollout plan (safe-by-default)
1) Immediate actions (day 0–2): apply Tier 0 mitigations; enable shadow routing to fp16 for 10% of production traffic on the targeted routes and monitor key metrics (regression rate, latency, cost).
2) Rapid validation (day 2–7): run augmented seed eval (including added numeric/calc tests) daily; hold a review checkpoint with SRE & infra if latency > SLO or cost > budget threshold.
3) Mid-term (day 7–21): implement prompt scaffolds & tokenization CI; run A/B rollout to 25/75 split if stable.
4) Longer-term (day 21+): plan micro-finetune + kernel fallback as a tracked engineering epic.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria
- Primary signal: onboarding eval regression rate <= 1.5% relative to baseline across the augmented seed set.
- Secondary signals: customer shadow test pass rate +0.5% improvement, numeric micro-test pass rate >= 98%, latency P95 within 1.2x of baseline for routed traffic.
- Safety gates: any increase in hallucination rate > 0.5% requires immediate rollback of the mitigation that caused it.

Open questions / things to validate
- How many unique instruction tokens changed across quant build? Action: engineering to run tokenization diff CI (see linked GH_PR).
- Are we comfortable with the cost delta of routing to fp16 for numeric-heavy routes? Run a 48 hr cost sim.
- Could the reranker introduce latency spikes for extreme long outputs? Add time budget and tail-monitoring to the reranker.

Action items (owners and near-term ETA)
- Miguel: implement route-by-tag policy + shadow routing (ETA: 48 hrs) (JIRA: MLONB-1421).
- Rina: add numeric micro-tests to eval harness + run 24h sweep (ETA: 72 hrs) (JIRA: EVAL-788).
- Ethan: tokenization CI and token-diff report for quant vs fp16 (ETA: 5 days) (GH_PR: see linked).
- Aisha: coordinate customer-facing note and internal postmortem update for execs (ETA: 7 days).

Appendix: sample exemplar cases (short)
- Case A (Context drop): long regulatory clause pasted by user; expected to reference clause id; model omitted clause and used generic template. Human label: FAIL.
- Case B (Numeric instability): table of expenses; model rolled up totals incorrectly (off by factor 10). Automated numeric check failed.
- Case C (Safe-mode overshoot): product-help prompt previously returned the steps; current returned a refusal with generic apology.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally operational: please add inline comments with experimental results and link template examples in Confluence. If you disagree with a mitigation priority, add a counter-proposal and estimated cost.

-- end --
